feature: Agentic Loop specification: redefine as 7-stage pipeline (ProblemStatement → BugAttributionReport) in system-specification.md and evaluation-framework.md
problem: The current system-specification.md treats the 'Agent Loop' as only the LLM turn-taking (stages 1-5) and puts Evidence Scoring and Report Assembly as separate 'post-loop' sections. This misframes the architecture: the agentic loop is the ENTIRE investigation — from ProblemStatement to BugAttributionReport — composed of 7 stages with explicit owners (LLM or Script). The docs say 'post-loop' but the code runs everything inside investigate().
proposed_solution: Rewrite the 'Agent Loop' + 'Evidence Scoring (Post-Loop)' sections as a single 'Agentic Loop' section with 7 enumerated stages. Each stage gets: owner, input, output, what happens (grounded in code), and the evaluation dimension that measures it. Also add a stage-to-metric mapping table in evaluation-framework.md.

1_problem_analysis.output: Identified file names, class names, error messages, component names (implicit in first LLM response)
1_problem_analysis.evaluation_dimension: N/A (no separate metric; quality propagates to search)

2_search.output: Set of candidate commit SHAs discovered via search/blame/log tools

3_examine.output: Diff content + commit messages for suspects
3_examine.code_reference: Same tool execution loop; tools: get_commit_diff, get_commit_message, get_file_at_commit

4_refine.output: Narrowed suspect list with blame chains and cross-references
4_refine.code_reference: Same tool execution loop; tools: get_blame, search_commits_by_keyword

5_conclude.output: ```suspects``` JSON block: list[SuspectCommit] with commit_id, confidence, mechanism, evidence_quotes

7_report_assembly.input: suspects + evidence_scores + tool_trace + budget state + timing
7_report_assembly.evaluation_dimension: Structural correctness (tested via schema, not scored)

acceptance_criteria: AC1: system-specification.md has a single 'Agentic Loop' section (no separate 'Agent Loop' + 'Evidence Scoring (Post-Loop)' sections)

AC2: All 7 stages are enumerated with: stage number, name, owner (LLM or Script), input, output, and evaluation dimension. Stage 1 output must be labeled 'implicit LLM reasoning (not a structured artifact)' — not a code-produced output.

AC3: Each stage description is grounded in actual code — references function names in orchestrator.py and evidence_tagger.py (line numbers optional). Stages 2-4 must explicitly share one code path (investigate() tool loop) and be distinguished by typical tool types, not separate enforcement.
AC4: The Pipeline Overview (Stage 2 table) references the 7-stage agentic loop, not just 'LLM loop + evidence scoring + report assembly'

AC5: evaluation-framework.md contains a 'Stage-to-Metric Mapping' section. Retrieval Recall maps to stages 3-4 (tools with commit_id in tool_trace args: get_commit_diff, get_commit_message, get_file_at_commit) — NOT stage 2 search listing tools. Hit@k/MRR map to stage 5 (final suspect list). D3 maps to stage 5 with 'not yet implemented' status. D6 maps to stage 6.
AC6: Stages 1-5 are documented as advisory (LLM may interleave) — no implication of strict sequential enforcement
AC7: Resource limits (budget: tokens/cost/tool_calls via BudgetState.budget_exceeded; max_turns via orchestrator loop counter) span stages 1-5 collectively, not per-stage
AC8: Stages 6-7 are documented as unconditional (always run after LLM loop exits, regardless of exit condition)

AC9: All content from the old 'Agent Loop' and 'Evidence Scoring (Post-Loop)' sections is preserved under the new structure: loop mechanics pseudocode, three exit conditions, tool/suspect output formats, budget table, evidence cascade, special cases, metadata keys
edge_cases: EC1: Stages 1-5 are NOT strictly sequential — the LLM may interleave search, examine, and refine across turns. The 5-phase strategy is advisory text in the system prompt, not enforced code. The doc must not imply stage gates.
EC2: Resource limits span stages 1-5 as a whole (budget checked at turn start; max_turns=15 via separate loop counter), not per-stage. The doc must not suggest per-stage budgets.
EC3: Stage 5 (Conclude) may not happen — if budget is exceeded, max_turns reached, or LLM emits no tools/no suspects, the loop exits with empty suspects. Stages 6-7 still run.
EC4: Stage 6 handles edge cases: diff unavailable (rate=0.0), diff truncated + quote not found (UNVERIFIABLE), quote < 8 chars (not grounded), no quotes (rate=0.0). These must be documented.
EC5: Evidence scores (stage 6) are metadata only — they do NOT modify suspect rank or confidence. This must be explicit.
EC6: Retrieval recall (eval_metrics.py) only checks commit_id in tool_trace[].args — SHAs appearing only in search tool result text are NOT counted. Doc must state this precisely.
EC7: If a response contains both ```suspects``` and ```tool``` blocks, suspects take precedence — tools in that turn are not executed (orchestrator checks suspects before tool_calls).
EC8: Mid-batch tool-call budget cutoff: when max_tool_calls reached mid-batch, remaining tool calls in the batch get a budget-limit message but the loop continues to the next turn.
verification_method: Evaluator reads the updated docs and cross-checks: (1) each stage description matches the actual code flow in orchestrator.py (investigate() method), (2) evidence scoring details match evidence_tagger.py (score_suspect_evidence + quote_in_diff), (3) stage-to-metric mapping in evaluation-framework.md matches the metrics defined in eval_metrics.py, (4) AC9 preservation checklist — all details from old sections present in new structure
